thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — serving-prod: elevated 5xxs and node flaps detected in us-west-2. Pager fired to oncall. See initial error spikes in traces.

Tess (oncall): got the page, I'm on it. what’s the current customer impact?

incident-bot: ~250 requests/min failing at peak, approx 7% global error rate, concentrated in us-west-2. Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Some request failures show 'CUDA error: invalid device function' and others show OOM during model init.

Ana (eng-runtime): joining. I'm seeing repeated model-init failures for model alias rdx-1.1q8 on several pods — errors during artifact deserialization then immediate container restart. Logs show compile timeout for tvm kernels on some nodes.

Kevin (sre): are these new deploys? any artifact push earlier today?

Maria (infra): Yeah we rolled a quantized artifact 03:10 UTC to canary pool, then promoted at 03:35. Canary looked fine but rollout overlapped with autoscaling events.

Jordan (support): multiple customers DMing about 500s in US-W region. Customer-impact tier: partial degradation, some timeouts turned into 502/503.

Ana (eng-runtime): stack sample from a failing pod: ```
ERROR: deserialize_artifact: unexpected EOF while reading tensor buffer
Caused by: RuntimeError: artifact checksum mismatch
During TVM compile: timeout after 120s for kernel fusion pass
CUDA error: driver shutting down (code 719)
```

Tess (oncall): ok that looks like two correlated issues: bad artifact -> deserialization errors -> compile retries -> GPU driver instability -> container crash. Need short-term mitigation to stop cascade.

Kevin (sre): immediate mitigation idea: 1) pause rollout of new artifact 2) remove canary from load balancer 3) route traffic to fallback model variant (non-quantized) 4) throttle simultaneous warmups with a concurrency cap.

Ana (eng-runtime): agree. I can flip the rollout freeze and pin traffic to rdx-1.1 (float) in the router. Also push a temporary config to disable eager compilation on affected node pool.

Maria (infra): doing LB changes now — draining canary nodes and shifting traffic. Setting autoscaler min to current to avoid new nodes joining and triggering loads.

sre-bot: deploy-freeze applied by ana (eng-runtime). Lock ID: LF-350123.

Jordan (support): telling priority customers we're investigating; ETA unknown. Any idea how long rollback takes?

Ana (eng-runtime): rollback to previous artifact on the model catalog should be a quick config change — pushing now. If nodes still fail during cold loads we'll use staged warmup (delay starts).

Kevin (sre): also, add node-level eviction protect for pods to avoid thrashing. If driver is CTD (crash-to-desktop) we need to cordon bad hosts. I'm scanning node events.

Tess (oncall): cordon any host with repeated GPU driver restarts. Maria, can you list nodes with >2 driver restarts in last 10m?

Maria (infra): listing: gpu-node-18, gpu-node-21, gpu-node-22 each show kernel oops and nvidia-driver restarts. cordoning gpu-node-18 and -21 now.

Ana (eng-runtime): rollback confirmed. Model traffic switched to rdx-1.0 (non-quantized) at 03:45:40 UTC. Observability: error rate is trending down in 2 of 3 pods.

incident-bot: Note: automatic retry suppression active for affected routes to avoid thundering herd during warmup.

Kevin (sre): monitoring for residual 500s. If compile timeouts persist, we need to bump compile timeout or precompile the kernels offline and push prebuilt artifacts.

Jordan (support): pinging top affected customers with a status update: "We mitigated an issue affecting inference in us-west-2 by rolling back model artifact. Some requests may have seen 500s between 03:35–03:46. We’re investigating root cause and will follow up."

Tess (oncall): quick RCA notes while fresh: sequence was artifact promotion + autoscale surge -> multiple simultaneous cold loads -> artifact deserialization failures on some nodes (checksum mismatches) -> repeated compile retries -> GPU driver instability -> container restarts -> increased 5xxs. Primary contributor appears to be artifact packaging/transport on a subset of nodes and insufficient warmup pacing.

Ana (eng-runtime): follow-ups: 1) add artifact checksum validation in agent with earlier fail-open fallback to previous artifact 2) implement staged warmup gate controlling concurrent model inits per node 3) increase compile timeout to 300s and add telemetry to detect long compiles 4) add prebuilt-kernel fallback to avoid on-host compilation for new artifacts.

Kevin (sre): infra follow-ups: 1) make autoscaler respect warmup-threshold annotations to avoid scaling spikes 2) improve node cordon automation when driver flaps detected 3) add alert for artifact checksum mismatch rate.

Tess (oncall): handing off to next oncall at 04:00 UTC — summary: rollback completed, traffic stable on fallback model, node cordons applied, customers notified, must-do postmortem and action items assigned.

sre-bot: handoff scheduled. Next oncall: luis (oncall) at 04:00 UTC. Handoff note: see LF-350123 lock, rollback performed, affected nodes cordoned, follow-ups in eng-runtime and infra.

Jordan (support): keeping ticket open with affected customers; will escalate if any regressions.

Ana (eng-runtime): leaving trace links and dump of failing artifact checksums in the incident doc. will create a follow-up PR for staged warmup and prebuilt-kernel fallback.

Tess (oncall): thanks team. closing page for now — move to postmortem channel once RCA draft ready. :white_check_mark:
